teaching_carrier.ordinary_lowercase: Source a–s map in alphabetic order to the first19 signs in ordinary_signs; t–z map to q followed by the first7 ordinary signs. This is one general letter table, never a word table.
teaching_carrier.rare_character_rule: For zero-based index j in rare_characters_in_order, write y followed by rare_selectors[floor(j/8)] and rare_selectors[j mod 8]. All three marks are consumed as one source character. Unlisted source characters are outside this teaching edition and cause an explicit failure, never deletion or guessed replacement.
teaching_carrier.marker: r never occurs in the letter carrier and is reserved for the mechanism declared in this card.
teaching_carrier.source_contract: Inputs are nonempty source tokens separated by single spaces, with explicit paragraph breaks. Uppercase, listed punctuation and digits are retained by the rare-character table. Repeated whitespace and exact physical source lineation are outside the declared input contract; semantic words, word order and paragraph boundaries are retained. No lowercasing, grammatical normalization or expansion of ambiguous historical spelling is performed.
teaching_carrier.reader_cost: The learner must know the source language, its ordinary spellings, the26 lowercase entries and the entire listed rare-character table, plus the mechanism-specific table/rules. Rare-character escape can be slow and long; its cost is charged. Drawings are already familiar transcription-designated shapes, but their artificial assignment is not a native letter or word-value claim.
teaching_carrier.decoding: Parse ordinary single signs, q plus exactly one permitted letter selector, or y plus exactly two rare selectors; reject unused combinations. The distinct marker r cannot be confused with a spelled source character. Multi-letter transcription labels such as ch name one working drawing here, without claiming that native writing has independently established these atoms.

title: RAW UNREVIEWED: reversible marked function-word prefixes with fully spelled lexical hosts
summary: A fixed small list of source word spellings becomes explicitly marked prefixes to the following ordinary spelled token. Every joined original boundary is reconstructed mechanically. This is a concrete reversible member of an already investigated grouping family, not a claimed new frequency effect.

encode: Read exact case-sensitive source tokens in order. Hold the maximal consecutive run of tokens whose complete spellings are in the12-word list.

If a non-list token follows in the same paragraph, write r+selector for each held word in order, then spell that host token in full with the common carrier, all as one visible group. An empty run leaves an ordinary spelled token.
If a paragraph ends with a held run, write just its r+selector prefixes as one marker-only group. No host is invented and no prefix crosses a paragraph.

Non-list tokens must use ordinary full spelling. Listed tokens must use the marked branch. Punctuation attached to a token is retained: for example a listed word followed by a comma within the same token is not an exact list member.
decode: At the beginning of each group, consume successive r+selector pairs and expand each to its exact list spelling as a separate source word. Decode the remaining ordinary body, if any, as one further word.

An r after the ordinary body has begun, an unknown selector, or a dangling r is illegal. A marker-only group is legal only at paragraph end. Re-encode to reject noncanonical separate spelling of listed tokens.
Restore one ordinary source space between all recovered tokens. The grouping changes writing spaces, not source order, word content or grammatical scope.
design.single_new_and_repeat: A one-character non-list token is fully spelled. Every unfamiliar token is fully spelled without a new lexical entry. Repeated source characters are preserved. Repeated listed words produce repeated explicit prefix codes; repeated lexical words produce repeated spelled bodies. No repetition is silently copied or omitted.
design.line_handling: Physical wraps occur between whole groups and never reset prefix interpretation. A paragraph boundary closes any pending run. Long runs have no arbitrary cap, which is a real length liability; adding a cap would require a separately declared design.
design.constructive_example: Abstract teaching input 'und nicht salzen' becomes prefix('und')+prefix('nicht')+spell('salzen') in one group and decodes to all three original words. A paragraph containing only 'und nicht' ends in a legal marker-only group. No semantic resolution of negation or pronouns is performed.
design.learning_cost: The common character tables,12 exact word-to-selector entries, one pending-run rule and one explicit paragraph-end case. All other source vocabulary remains ordinary spelling. The12 shortcuts are an overt small codebook, not free assumed knowledge.
design.necessary_observable_difference: Every removed source word space corresponds to a written marked prefix; prefix order reproduces source order. The same marker must occur only in the leading run. Unmarked deletion of a boundary or arbitrary fusion of content words is forbidden.
design.smallest_falsifier: A human given only the tables must reconstruct a sentence with two successive prefix words, a homographic ordinary use, a new lexical host, punctuation and a final hostless run. One lost word/negative or alternate undecidable source tokenization fails. With a later fixed native marker binding, an occurrence after an ordinary body begins violates the lesson.
design.strongest_counterexample: Root's GDT1176 fixed P1–P3 grouping variants already failed the joint source-frequency gates. This card belongs to that family and cannot be selected merely because its reversible boundary carrier was spelled out. Long prefix runs can also create extreme written groups. Exact-word matching ignores grammatical function intentionally; it preserves any ambiguity instead of claiming a parser.
design.statistical_limit: No measured fit. The grouping can change token distributions, but marker and host costs must both be counted. Its12-word list was stated before receiving1176's numerical summary and is not adjusted to approach any gate.
